'''''Elaeocarpus decipiens''''', commonly known as '''Japanese blueberry tree''',<ref name="NC State">{{cite web |title=Elaeocarpus decipiens (Japanese Blueberry Tree) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/elaeocarpus-decipiens/ |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu |access-date=20 June 2024}}</ref> is a species of flowering tree in the family [[Elaeocarpaceae]]. It has red, brown, and green leaves that are typically egg-shaped, 5-petaled flowers ranging in color from cream to light pink, and small [[drupe]] fruit.

==Description==
''Elaeocarpus decipiens'' typically grows to {{Convert|30 to 40|ft}} in height.<ref name="NC State" /> Flowers bloom from late spring to early summer. These flowers can be white, cream, and light pink. Flowers are typically one inch or less in size and are often hidden within the foliage. The fruits are olive-shaped drupe fruits that are dark blue to black in color. The fruit is inedible and is less than one inch long.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Martin |first1=Chris |title=Elaeocarpus decipiens |url=https://www.public.asu.edu/~camartin/plants/Plant%20html%20files/elaeocarpusdecipiens.html |website=Virtual Library of Phoenix Landscape Plants |access-date=20 June 2024}}</ref><ref name="NC State" /> The leaves are egg-shaped. New foliage tends to be more red, while older foliage is closer to green.<ref name="NC State" />

==Distribution and habitat==
''Elaeocarpus decipiens'' originates from East Asia. The native range includes Southern China, Vietnam, Japan, Korea, and Taiwan.<ref name="POWO" /><ref name="NC State" /> The plant does well in USDA hardiness zones 8B to 10B and has a very high drought tolerance.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gilman |first1=Edward |title=Elaeocarpus decipens - Trees and Power Lines |url=https://hort.ifas.ufl.edu/treesandpowerlines/elaeocarpus_decipens.shtml |website=Trees and Power Lines - UF/IFAS |access-date=20 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100503104313/http://hort.ifas.ufl.edu/treesandpowerlines/elaeocarpus_decipens.shtml|archive-date=3 May 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref>
